clue.text: Deputy being investigated

definitions.meaning: a stand-in who learns a lead actor's part to cover for them
the phrase '...' means being examined or looked into

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre stand-in deputises for a principal actor, while 'under study' is the idiom for being examined.

clue.text: University expert on Arabia makes great fuss

parts.note: a pro is an expert
AR is an abbreviation for Arabia or Arabic

explanation.surface: An academic specialist on the Middle East causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud public commotion or outcry.

clue.text: Rat's fault

definitions.meaning: to rat is to desert one's side, turn traitor

explanation.definitionFit: To defect is to desert to the other side, like a rat, and a defect is a flaw.

clue.text: A friar involved with Satanism cult

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the friar and Satanism letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A monk gets mixed up with devil worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges A FRIAR with SATANISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Rastafarianism is a Jamaican religious movement, here loosely called a cult.

clue.text: Watch Cable perhaps entertaining European politician that is Conservative

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the tie word holds the other pieces

parts.note: a cable can serve as a tie, binding things together; perhaps marks it as an example
MEP is a Member of the European Parliament
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Watch Vince Cable host a European politician who is a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' looks like Vince Cable, a British Liberal Democrat politician, but means a tie; 'entertaining' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a portable timepiece, an instrument for telling the time.

clue.text: Last month's indication of alternative scenery

parts.note: December, DEC, is the last month of the year
or is the word that signals an alternative

explanation.surface: Last month's signal pointed to a different landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the theatrical term for stage scenery and setting.

clue.text: Turned crazy making attempt

indicators.note: turned means the word for crazy is read backwards, end to start

parts.note: bats is informal British for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: Someone went mad while trying something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses BATS (crazy) to give the answer; 'making' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is the idiom for making an attempt.

clue.text: Made series of tweets about answer put to test

indicators.note: about means the bird-song word goes around the answer abbreviation

parts.note: a bird that trilled made a run of tweets

explanation.surface: Someone posted a run of social media messages about a reply being tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tweets' suggests social media but means birdsong. 'about' puts A inside TRILLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Trialled means tested, tried out before wider use.

clue.text: Provide with extra security except for lock

parts.note: but means except, as in all but one
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Fit extra security to everything except the door lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door fitting but means a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttress is to support or reinforce, giving extra strength.

clue.text: Items quickly delivered top job

definitions.meaning: letters sent by the faster, pricier Royal Mail service
a first-class position, a post of the highest grade

explanation.walkthrough: First-class post is the faster tier of the British Royal Mail service.
explanation.definitionFit: First-class post is priority mail, and a first-class post is a top-grade job.

clue.text: Redhead with animal skin upset you and me

indicators.note: upset in a down-turned sense: the word for animal skin is turned back to front

parts.note: fur is an animal's hairy coat or skin
us is the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired person wearing a fur coat upsets a pair of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' in a down-style sense turns the skin word around; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rufus is a Latin-derived name meaning red-haired, famously the nickname of King William II.

clue.text: Factory worker producing cars on time collecting a high honour

indicators.note: collecting means the car-and-time letters gather up the other pieces inside them

parts.note: Minis are small British cars
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a high British award

explanation.surface: A factory hand turns out cars punctually and is given a top award.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British award; 'collecting' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A machinist operates machines, typically on a factory floor or in a workshop.

clue.text: A gaffer's last to fix bright light

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word gaffer's

parts.note: to clamp is to fix something firmly in place

explanation.surface: A film set's chief electrician fixes up a powerful lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: A gaffer is the chief lighting electrician on a film set, which suits the surface; here only its last letter, R, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp produces intense light from an electric arc between electrodes.

clue.text: Person in charge round street is thief

indicators.note: round means the leader's word is placed around the street abbreviation

parts.note: a ruler is a person in charge

explanation.surface: Someone in authority on a street turns out to be a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the container; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler is a thief, specifically one who steals cattle or horses.

clue.text: These criminals sound mad

parts.note: sound in the sense secure or undamaged means safe
crackers is informal British for mad

explanation.surface: Lawbreakers who sound insane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a homophone signal but is an adjective meaning secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Safecrackers are criminals who break open safes to steal their contents.

clue.text: Withdrawn US leader once backing British one

indicators.note: backing means the US leader's name is read backwards

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was a former US president
Ted Heath was a former British prime minister

explanation.surface: A former American president withdrew support for a British counterpart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but signals the reversal of the American name only; Ted Heath was the British PM of the early 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Retracted means taken back or withdrawn, as of a statement.

clue.text: Second old record making splash

parts.note: platter is old slang for a gramophone record

explanation.surface: A second vintage disc becomes a big hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To splatter is to splash with drops of liquid.

clue.text: A lost animal's outside hospital — dog ends in there

indicators.note: outside means the lost animal's word sits around the hospital abbreviation

parts.note: a stray is a lost animal, and the possessive stray's gives the letters

explanation.surface: A lost animal is outside the vet's, and a dog finishes inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Dog-ends is British slang for cigarette butts, not a dog's ends. 'outside' puts STRAYS around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashtrays are receptacles where cigarette butts are stubbed out and left.

clue.text: A little snipe playing up causing trouble

indicators.note: playing up means behaving badly, so these letters misbehave into a new order

explanation.surface: A small wading bird misbehaves and makes a nuisance of itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing up' rearranges the twelve letters of A LITTLE SNIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilential is used loosely for annoying or troublesome, like a plague.

clue.text: Sportsman to get cross holding line

indicators.note: holding means the cross word contains the line abbreviation

parts.note: to anger is to make cross

explanation.surface: A sportsman gets angry while gripping his line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts L inside ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler fishes with rod and line, a sporting pursuit.

clue.text: Hurl abuse at son on shelf

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A father shouts insults at his son perched on a ledge.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to sledge is to taunt a batsman verbally.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledging is cricket slang for insulting an opponent to unsettle them.

clue.text: Eulogist for Caesar, J? The opposite

definitions.meaning: Mark Antony delivered Caesar's funeral speech
a word of opposite meaning to another

explanation.walkthrough: The format 'Caesar, J' (surname, initial) tells you to write the eulogist the same way: ANTONY, M.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word meaning the reverse of another, as hot is to cold.

clue.text: Antipodean to wander around over island

indicators.note: around means the wandering word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: to roam is to wander

explanation.surface: An Australasian traveller roams about an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the reversal; in this down clue 'over' places it above the island letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous people of New Zealand, an Antipodean land.

clue.text: Football team succeeded in stadium with skill finally

indicators.note: in means the succession abbreviation is set within the stadium word

parts.note: an arena is a stadium
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of skill

explanation.surface: A football club wins at its ground thanks to skill at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside ARENA; 'finally' gives L from skill. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a well-known English Premier League football club based in north London.

clue.text: What IOC did after tournament's opening to delight

indicators.note: after means the IOC phrase follows the tournament's opening letter
opening means just the first letter of tournament's is used

parts.note: the International Olympic Committee runs sport, so it ran sport

explanation.surface: Olympic organisers staged events after a tournament began, to everyone's pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with strong emotion, especially joy.

clue.text: Drunk was working having missed start

indicators.note: having missed start means the first letter of the working word is dropped

parts.note: toiled means worked hard

explanation.surface: A drunk was at work but turned up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having missed start' drops T from TOILED.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is informal slang for drunk, well lubricated with alcohol.

clue.text: Spots dare-devil

definitions.meaning: a breakout of red spots on the skin
reckless, acting without thought of danger

explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of skin spots, and rash also describes reckless, foolhardy behaviour.

clue.text: A tired peer resorted to second home

indicators.note: resorted read as re-sorted means these letters are sorted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A weary lord retreated to his holiday house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorted' rearranges A TIRED PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-a-terre is a small second residence kept in a city for occasional use.
